derivedFrom.note: mtime only; no wall-clock timestamp is written

labels.label: accelerating
nonClaims: Third-to-third ratios are sensitive to where the cuts happen to fall and to false candidates.
Does not show a smooth ramp, a musical build, or a deliberate escalation.

labels.label: burst-texture
nonClaims: A burst of candidate events is not a verified rapid sequence; it can be motion or luminance artefacts.
Does not establish a montage, a chase, a stinger or any narrative function.

labels.label: decelerating
nonClaims: Third-to-third ratios are sensitive to where the cuts happen to fall and to false candidates.
Does not show a fade-out, a slow ending, or a deliberate release of tension.

labels.label: long-take
nonClaims: A low detected-event rate is not a verified take length: missed cuts shorten apparent shots and false candidates split them.
Does not establish that the camera holds, that the action is continuous, or that the shot is the editorial unit.

labels.label: rapid-montage
nonClaims: Fast movement, flashes, strobe and compression can inflate the candidate count, so a high rate is not proof of rapid editing.
Does not establish shot count, transition type, pace change within the runtime or editorial intent.

labels.label: single-shot
nonClaims: Does not prove the work has a single shot: an undetected cut, a locked-off long take and a continuous generated image all produce the same scan.
Does not establish camera movement, subject continuity or editorial intent.

labels.label: steady-cut
nonClaims: Describes a candidate-event rate over the runtime, not a rhythmic pattern, beat alignment or editing philosophy.
Does not distinguish hard cuts from fades, dissolves, flashes or false candidates.

labels.label: strobe-texture
nonClaims: Not an editing label: strobe texture can come from flashing content inside a shot, from a strobe light, or from compression artefacts.
Not a photic-safety measurement: the 1 Hz appearance series aliases higher frequencies and cannot certify a flash rate.

labels.label: flicker-high
nonClaims: Not a flicker frequency or a flash-rate measurement; the 1 Hz series aliases content above roughly 1 Hz.
Does not identify strobing, flashing, lightning, camera shake or an effect.

labels.label: flicker-low
nonClaims: A low sampled instability value does not mean the image is still, nor that the shot is locked off.
Cadence aliases fast variation, so low values can coexist with visible flicker.

labels.label: luma-fall
nonClaims: A fitted downward drift is not a fade, a blackout, or a deliberate tonal arc.
R-squared is fit quality over 1 Hz samples, not evidence of causation or continuity.

labels.label: luma-rise
nonClaims: A fitted upward drift is not a creative brightening, a reveal, or a deliberate tonal arc.
R-squared is fit quality over 1 Hz samples, not evidence of causation or continuity.

labels.label: static-frame-dominant
nonClaims: A static appearance pair is not a static camera or a still frame; slow motion and long dissolves can also change little per second.
Does not establish a freeze, a title card or a held composition.

labels.label: loud-mix
nonClaims: A loud integrated level is not loudness compliance, clarity, impact or a quality verdict.
The value is a programme-loudness measurement of one mixed stream; it says nothing about dialogue, music or effects separately.

labels.label: loudness-fall
nonClaims: A fitted loudness fall is not a release, a fade, a breakdown or a deliberate energy arc.
R-squared is fit quality across the runtime, not evidence of causation or listener-perceived change.

labels.label: loudness-rise
nonClaims: A fitted loudness rise is not a build, a crescendo, a drop or a deliberate energy arc.
R-squared is fit quality across the runtime, not evidence of causation or listener-perceived change.

labels.label: narrow-lra
nonClaims: A narrow range is not a loudness-war verdict, a format convention or a quality judgement.
Does not show that the record is dynamically flat to a listener or that the mix is consistent in intent.

labels.label: onset-dense
nonClaims: Onsets are amplitude-envelope rises, not musical beats, cuts, hits or speech events.
Dense onset detection can come from percussive music, speech, noise or effects; no source separation is performed.

labels.label: onset-sparse
nonClaims: Sparse onsets are not silence, a drone, an ambient score, or a deliberate restraint.
The detector is causal and threshold-based; sustained sounds with smooth attacks can yield few onsets.

labels.label: quiet-mix
nonClaims: A quiet integrated level is not intimacy, restraint, a mix defect or a quality verdict.
Records at or below the -70 LUFS gate are reported as at-or-below-gate and receive no loudness band.

labels.label: silent-tail
nonClaims: Tail silence may be an artefact of the rendition, the encode, or the source's own end card, not an editorial choice.
Does not establish an ending, a button, a fade-out or a pause in the narrative.

labels.label: wide-lra
nonClaims: Loudness range is a statistical spread of short-term loudness, not a dynamic-style, genre or quality judgement.
Does not localise the loud and quiet passages, and does not establish a build or a drop.

labels.label: centre-weighted-motion
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a centre-heavy change distribution is not a subject position, a composition or a compositional intent.

labels.label: dissolve-using
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, short and long dissolve classes do not establish a specific transition effect, direction or intent.

labels.label: fade-using
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a recovered luma dip or peak does not establish a fade to black or white as an edit.

labels.label: hard-cut-dominant
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, the transition classes are fixed proxies that can confuse flashes, fast motion and compression with edits.

labels.label: overlay-active
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, high-frequency luma volatility does not identify text, a logo, a lower-third, a title or any graphic element.

labels.label: pan-dominant
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a pan fraction cannot separate camera, subject and post moves, and parallax or zooms violate the translation model.

labels.label: static-camera
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a majority of static translation pairs does not establish a static camera, a locked-off rig, or an absence of internal subject motion.

labels.label: building
nonClaims: Building does not mean a narrative build, a musical crescendo, a rising action or an intended climax.
The label is a conjunction of a pace ratio and one fitted appearance or loudness slope; each component retains its own caveats.

labels.label: flat-steady
nonClaims: Flat-steady does not mean calm, restrained, contemplative or monotonous.
A flat appearance fit and a steady pace ratio can coexist with strong internal motion, colour change or loud audio events.

labels.label: front-loaded
nonClaims: Front-loaded does not mean a hook, a cold open, a trailer structure or an audience-retention tactic.
The composite is a conjunction of measured rate ratios, not an editorial reading of the opening.

labels.label: animation-style
nonClaims: Does not identify stop-motion, CG, cel, collage, mixed media, hand-drawn or any other technique.
Would require labelled frames or a trained, validated classifier with documented error rates.

labels.label: authorship
nonClaims: Does not identify a director, studio, animator, tool or generative model.
Would require provenance metadata or a validated authorship-attribution method with a stated error rate.

labels.label: camera-rig-inference
nonClaims: Does not establish a dolly, crane, handheld, gimbal, drone or locked-off camera.
Would require EXIF/rig metadata or a validated camera-motion model with calibrated ambiguity handling.

labels.label: genre
nonClaims: Does not identify music video, commercial, title sequence, brand film, trailer or any other genre.
Would require a labelled genre corpus or the catalog's own editorial categories, used as a separate field.

labels.label: intent
nonClaims: Does not establish why a choice was made, what a client asked for, or what a sequence is meant to achieve.
Would require creator interviews, briefs or a labelled intent study with documented coding rules.

labels.label: quality
nonClaims: Does not rank records, measure craft, predict awards or establish audience response.
Would require a defined rubric, trained raters and an inter-rater reliability statistic.

labels.label: transition-ground-truth
nonClaims: Does not establish that a cut occurred at a frame, that a dissolve lasted a stated time, or that a fade reached black.
Would require frame-accurate human annotation with an inter-annotator agreement statistic.

labels.label: vfx-effect-identity
nonClaims: Does not identify blur, glow, grain, distortion, particles, keying or any compositing operation.
Would require an effect-labelled dataset and a validated detector, plus a stated confusion matrix.

labels.label: video-template-detection
nonClaims: Does not identify a reusable package, a design system, a template family or a campaign system.
Would require a template library plus a matcher with a measured false-positive rate.

notes: A label is a predicate over stored numeric evidence, not a creative archetype.
Cut candidates are ffmpeg scene-score exceedances; fast motion, flashes and compression can inflate them.
Layer B and the appearance component of layer E come from the 1 Hz stored series, so they are sampled, not full-rate.
Layer D is specified against motionProfile.* but no stored record carries it; nothing in layer D is assigned.
Layer F names are non-assignable by construction and have assigned: 0.
No quality, genre, intent, authorship or effect-identity claim is made anywhere in this file.
